summary: uzair-rajput-new CJS entry decrypts and executes hidden payload on require()
details: The package advertises itself as a gradient-string colorizer. The ESM entry (dist/index.js / dist/index.mjs) implements that stated purpose in plain source. The CommonJS entry (dist/index.cjs), which is loaded on any `require('uzair-rajput-new')`, does something entirely different: it reconstructs a 32-byte AES key by XOR-decoding byte arrays split across three sibling files (dist/_a.cjs masked with 17, dist/_b.cjs with 91, dist/_c.cjs with 53), derives the final key via scryptSync using the hardcoded salt 'uzair-rajput-salt-2024', AES-256-CBC-decrypts an embedded ~5KB base64 ciphertext, and executes the decrypted plaintext with `new Function('module','exports','require','__dirname','__filename', _x)` — giving the hidden payload full access to require, fs, net, child_process, and the module's exports at load time. The split-key obfuscation, the clean-ESM / trojanized-CJS decoy split, and the encrypted payload delivery form a deliberate anti-analysis pattern; a gradient colorizer has no legitimate need for AES-decrypted, dynamically-evaluated bytecode gated behind CommonJS consumers.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
